title_en: This US House district was once a political battleground. Now it shows why Congress is dysfunctional
title_zh: 这个美国众议院选区曾经是一个政治战场。现在它显示了为什么国会功能失调
summary: The number of politically competitive U.S. House seats is shrinking rapidly
summary_zh: 美国众议院政治竞争席位数量正在迅速减少
body_en: This US House district was once a political battleground. Now it shows why Congress is dysfunctional - ABC News
This US House district was once a political battleground. Now it shows why Congress is dysfunctional
The number of politically competitive U.S. House seats is shrinking rapidly

RALEIGH, N.C. -- In 2022, Democrat Wiley Nickel ran as a moderate and narrowly won North Carolina's 13th Congressional District by about 9,000 votes. Two years later, the current congressman, Republican Brad Knott, ran as a conservative and coasted into the U.S. House by more than 70,000 votes.
Voters didn't change their minds. Politicians changed their voters.

The Republican-controlled legislature redrew the state's congressional map to transform what was one of the last remaining swing districts in the South to a safe GOP seat. Lawmakers split the rectangular 13th District into an hourglass shape that carved out Democratic voters in Raleigh and replaced them with a swath of rural counties reaching up to the Virginia border.

Swing seats, meaning a district that a presidential candidate won by 5 percentage points or fewer in the previous election, are disappearing from the national map. For decades after World War II, the number of competitive seats in the House slowly eroded as the United States grew more polarized , voters were less likely to split their ticket between parties and people moved closer to like-minded neighbors, creating Democratic strongholds in urban areas and Republicans ones across rural America.

That decline accelerated over the past year after Republican President Donald Trump sparked a partisan redistricting battle. The number of swing districts fell from 45 to 37. There were 96 House seats that fit the modern definition of a swing seat in 1964, according to one count from the 1970s, when the shrinking number of such districts was first noted.
That means the overwhelming majority of House seats are effectively won in primaries , with the support of only a fraction of voters who usually are at the extreme ideological end of their party.
Nickel saw the impact firsthand during his lone term in Washington.

“The biggest divide I found in Congress wasn’t Democrat versus Republican, it was safe seats versus competitive seats,” Nickel said. “When your focus is on running a campaign where you talk to every single voter, you look at things differently and your focus is on solving problems.”
Unite America, an organization pushing alternatives to party primaries, calculated that 87% of the representatives elected to the House in 2024 were chosen by 7% of the country’s voters.

“Voters don’t have any way of holding Congress responsible, except for a narrow window of swing districts,” Nick Troiano, the group's executive director, said in an interview, adding that he expects things to get worse in November. “The least competitive election of our lifetimes will lead to the least accountable and least representative Congress of our lifetimes.”
Republicans are hoping the smaller number of competitive seats puts a low ceiling on what Democrats can win on Nov. 3.
“Both sides are fighting over a narrow House battlefield,” said Mike Marinella, a spokesman for the National Republican Congressional Campaign. “It's a knife fight in a dark alley.”
The alley may be widening this year , but it still is an alley.

Democrats have expanded their political targets, given the unpopular war with Iran and voters angry about high prices. Both parties are spending on campaigns in Republican area that normally would not be competitive.
Even in what is shaping up as a difficult political environment, however, Republicans are protected by the limited number of seats in play.
“Even if there's the kind of swing we got in 2006, there's not going to be 40 seats changing hands. There's going to be 20 seats changing hands,” said Ian Shapiro, a Yale political scientist.

There is a long-standing debate among academics as to how much of the decline can be blamed on partisan-motivated redistricting , known as gerrymandering, and how much on Americans' increasing proclivity to live among like-minded people who vote the same way. Multiple studies have found that without partisan gerrymandering, the House would have about double the number of competitive seats it has now.
body_zh: 这个美国众议院选区曾经是一个政治战场。现在它显示了国会功能失调的原因 - ABC News
这个美国众议院选区曾经是一个政治战场。现在它显示了为什么国会功能失调
美国众议院政治竞争席位数量正在迅速减少
北卡罗来纳州罗利——2022 年，民主党人威利·尼克尔 (Wiley Nickel) 作为温和派参选，以约 9,000 票微弱优势赢得北卡罗来纳州第 13 国会选区。两年后，现任国会议员、共和党人布拉德·诺特以保守派身份参选，并以超过 7 万票的优势进入美国众议院。
选民没有改变主意。政客们改变了他们的选民。
共和党控制的立法机构重新绘制了该州的国会地图，将南部仅存的摇摆选区之一转变为共和党的安全席位。立法者将长方形的第 13 选区分割成沙漏形状，将罗利的民主党选民划出，并用延伸至弗吉尼亚州边境的一大片乡村县取而代之。
摇摆席位，即总统候选人在上次选举中以 5 个百分点或更少的优势赢得的选区，正在从国家地图上消失。第二次世界大战后的几十年里，随着美国两极分化加剧，众议院的竞争性席位数量慢慢减少，选民们不太可能在党派之间分配选票，人们也更加接近志同道合的邻居，从而在城市地区建立了民主党的据点，在美国农村地区建立了共和党的据点。
在共和党总统唐纳德·特朗普引发党派重新划分选区之战后，这种下降在过去一年加速。摇摆选区的数量从 45 个减少到 37 个。根据 1970 年代的一项统计，1964 年，众议院有 96 个席位符合摇摆席位的现代定义，当时此类选区的数量首次出现减少。
这意味着绝大多数众议院席位实际上是在初选中赢得的，而只有一小部分选民的支持，而这些选民通常处于党派的极端意识形态一端。
尼克尔在华盛顿的唯一任期内亲眼目睹了这一影响。
“我在国会发现的最大分歧不是民主党与共和党，而是安全席位与竞争性席位，”尼克尔说。 “当你的重点是开展一场与每一位选民交谈的竞选活动时，你会以不同的方式看待事物，你的重点是解决问题。”
推动政党初选替代方案的组织Unite America计算出，2024年当选的众议院代表中有87%是由该国7%的选民选出的。
该组织执行董事尼克·特罗伊亚诺(Nick Troiano)在接受采访时表示，“除了摇摆选区的狭窄窗口之外，选民没有任何办法让国会承担责任。”他补充说，他预计11月情况会变得更糟。 “我们一生中竞争最激烈的选举将导致我们一生中最不负责任和最具代表性的国会。”
共和党人希望竞争性席位数量较少，从而降低民主党在 11 月 3 日获胜的上限。
“双方都在狭小的众议院战场上展开战斗，”全国共和党国会竞选活动发言人迈克·马里内拉 (Mike Marinella) 说。 “这是在黑暗的小巷里进行的一场刀战。”
今年胡同可能会拓宽，但它仍然是胡同。
鉴于与伊朗的战争不受欢迎以及选民对高物价感到愤怒，民主党扩大了他们的政治目标。两党都在共和党地区的竞选活动上投入资金，而这些竞选活动通常不会具有竞争力。
然而，即使在当前艰难的政治环境中，共和党人仍受到有限席位的保护。
“即使出现 2006 年那样的摇摆，也不会有 40 个席位易手。将会有 20 个席位易手，”耶鲁大学政治学家伊恩·夏皮罗 (Ian Shapiro) 表示。
学术界长期以来一直存在争论，即选民人数下降在多大程度上可以归咎于党派动机的选区重新划分，即所谓的不公正划分选区，以及美国人越来越倾向于生活在志同道合、投票方式相同的人中间。多项研究发现，如果没有党派不公正的选区划分，众议院的竞争性席位数量将是现在的两倍左右。

title_en: Sexual harassment rules for Congress are under review after a flurry of ethics cases
title_zh: 在发生一系列道德案件后，国会的性骚扰规则正在接受审查
summary: Lawmakers reviewing the issue of sexual harassment on Capitol Hill say they're disturbed by what they've found
summary_zh: 在国会山审查性骚扰问题的立法者表示，他们对所发现的情况感到不安
body_en: Sexual harassment rules for Congress are under review after a flurry of ethics cases - ABC News
Sexual harassment rules for Congress are under review after a flurry of ethics cases
Lawmakers reviewing the issue of sexual harassment on Capitol Hill say they're disturbed by what they've found

WASHINGTON -- When Rep. Kat Cammack began work on a task force this spring to combat sexual misconduct on Capitol Hill , the Florida Republican soon heard from former staffers who wanted to share their stories.
They “came out of the woodwork” she said, and had stayed silent because it was well established that coming forward would be the end of a career they had worked so hard to achieve.
“Those were some of the hardest conversations to have," Cammack said. "And the stories were gut-wrenching."

This year's spike in House Ethics Committee investigations related to sexual misconduct prompted congressional leaders to set up a working group led by Cammack and Rep. Teresa Leger Fernandez, D-N.M. What they have found is disturbing, Cammack said.

Victims are unclear about where they can go for help. They do not trust there will be repercussions for the perpetrator. And the current requirements for reporting harassment can work against them, such as a 180-day “shot clock” for filing a claim after an alleged violation.
“It's a disaster," Cammack said. “The entire system on Capitol Hill is really designed to create a chilling effect for victims."
The task force is expected to release recommended changes after the Nov. 3 elections with a goal of taking action before the end of the year.

In a Congress that has generally struggled this year to do more than keep the federal government running, the House Ethics Committee has been caught in the middle of the some of the biggest stories coming out of Washington.

Three lawmakers resigned this year rather than face the prospect of an expulsion vote. Two of those cases involved alleged sexual misconduct. Another member was censured for his interactions with two female aides on his staff. Other investigations are ongoing.

Those stories emerged at a time when Congress was confronted by public outrage over the government's handling of the Jeffrey Epstein case. In the previous months, members of the Democratic Women's Caucus had multiple meetings with survivors who were pushing for the release of Epstein-related files at the Department of Justice.

In April, the Ethics Committee began an investigation into whether then-Rep. Eric Swalwell , D-Calif., engaged in sexual misconduct toward an employee working under his supervision. Swalwell would soon resign as colleagues called for his expulsion.

Similarly, Rep. Tony Gonzales , R-Texas, resigned as the committee investigated whether he had engaged in sexual misconduct toward an employee in his office. Gonzales had acknowledged an affair with a staff member who later died by suicide.

Most recently, the committee recommended the censure of Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., following an investigation that concluded he engaged in persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct toward two young female staffers in his office. The House went along with the recommendation by a vote of 413-2.

Rep. Jimmy Gomez, D-Calif., is also the subject of a committee investigation that he may have engaged in sexual misconduct with a House staffer. Gomez said he would cooperate with the investigation but also stressed that his actions were consensual in nature and did not violate the law or House Ethics rules. He also apologized to his family and constituents.

The committee is also investigating whether Rep. Cory Mills, R-Fla., engaged in sexual misconduct or dating violence, among other allegations. Mills has denied the allegations and recently lost a Republican primary.

Cammack said that as stories began to surface about some of the cases before the committee, she and colleagues began talking about what they could do to “clean up the House.” She approached Speaker Mike Johnson , R-La., about getting on board.

body_zh: 在发生一系列道德案件后，国会的性骚扰规则正在接受审查 - ABC News
在发生一系列道德案件后，国会的性骚扰规则正在接受审查
在国会山审查性骚扰问题的立法者表示，他们对所发现的情况感到不安
华盛顿——当众议员凯特·卡马克今年春天开始组建一个打击国会山不当性行为的特别工作组时，这位佛罗里达州共和党人很快就收到了前工作人员的来信，他们希望分享自己的故事。
她说，他们“从木制品中脱颖而出”，并保持沉默，因为众所周知，站出来将是他们辛辛苦苦取得的职业生涯的终结。
“这些是最难进行的对话，”卡马克说。 “这些故事令人心痛。”
今年众议院道德委员会有关不当性行为的调查激增，促使国会领导人成立了一个由卡马克和新墨西哥州众议员特蕾莎·莱杰·费尔南德斯领导的工作组。卡马克说，他们的发现令人不安。
受害者不清楚可以去哪里寻求帮助。他们不相信肇事者会受到惩罚。目前举报骚扰的要求可能对他们不利，例如在涉嫌违规后提出索赔有 180 天的“限制”。
“这是一场灾难，”卡马克说。 “国会山的整个系统实际上是为了给受害者制造寒蝉效应。”
该工作组预计将在 11 月 3 日选举后发布修改建议，目标是在年底前采取行动。
今年国会除了维持联邦政府的运转之外，还一直在努力做更多的事情，而众议院道德委员会却卷入了华盛顿发生的一些重大事件的中间。
今年，三名议员辞职，以免面临驱逐投票的前景。其中两起案件涉及涉嫌不当性行为。另一名成员因与两名女助手的互动而受到谴责。其他调查正在进行中。
这些故事出现之际，国会正面临公众对政府处理杰弗里·爱泼斯坦案的愤怒。在过去的几个月里，民主妇女核心小组的成员与幸存者举行了多次会议，她们推动司法部公布与爱泼斯坦相关的文件。
四月，道德委员会开始调查当时的众议员是否。加利福尼亚州民主党人埃里克·斯瓦尔韦尔 (Eric Swalwell) 对在他监督下工作的一名员工实施了不当性行为。斯瓦尔韦尔很快就辞职了，因为同事们呼吁将他开除。
同样，德克萨斯州共和党众议员托尼·冈萨雷斯(Tony Gonzales)辞职，因为委员会正在调查他是否对办公室的一名员工有不当性行为。冈萨雷斯承认与一名工作人员有染，该工作人员后来自杀身亡。
最近，委员会建议对北卡罗来纳州共和党众议员查克·爱德华兹（Chuck Edwards）进行谴责，调查得出结论，他对办公室的两名年轻女职员持续存在不专业和不当的行为。众议院以 413 票对 2 票通过了这项建议。
加利福尼亚州民主党众议员吉米·戈麦斯也是委员会调查的对象，因为他可能与众议院工作人员发生了不当性行为。戈麦斯表示，他将配合调查，但也强调，他的行为本质上是双方同意的，没有违反法律或众议院道德规则。他还向家人和选民道歉。
该委员会还在调查佛罗里达州共和党众议员科里·米尔斯是否存在不当性行为或约会暴力等指控。米尔斯否认了这些指控，并在最近的共和党初选中落败。
卡马克说，随着委员会审理的一些案件的故事开始浮出水面，她和同事们开始讨论他们可以采取哪些措施来“清理众议院”。她向路易斯安那州共和党众议员迈克·约翰逊寻求加入的机会。

Russian operatives are pumping out fabricated claims about Democratic candidates, AI-manipulated videos of celebrities and fake posts impersonating real news outlets in an effort to influence American voters in the final run-up to Election Day.

Researchers who track online influence operations and lawmakers who've been briefed by the intelligence community say Kremlin-backed groups are renewing familiar tactics they've used to sow distrust and discord in previous elections in the U.S. and around the world.
Top 2 Democrats on Intel say they're preparing for Trump to claim foreign meddling

"It's a carnival out there," Rep. Jim Himes of Connecticut , the ranking member on the House intelligence committee, told reporters this week. "They're throwing everything out there to generate a sense of chaos and anarchy."
The goal is to exacerbate divisions, erode confidence in democracy and, crucially, undermine U.S. support for Ukraine.

"At the end of the day, the main issue for Russia is and has to be Ukraine," said Darren Linvill, co-director of Clemson University's Media Forensics Hub, who has tracked foreign propaganda campaigns for years.

Linvill says the Russian playbook is consistent. A false claim or divisive narrative is seeded on social media or on a fake website posing as a news organization or think tank. It's spread by state media, automated fake accounts or, increasingly, paid influencers, in the hopes that it gets seen and repeated by real people.

"In the same way that marketing companies will pay an influencer to disseminate, you know, 'Nike's a great shoe,' the Russians do it with false information and made-up lies," he said. "They use influencers that know their audience, that are part of that audience, and they know how to give that audience a message that they want to hear," Linvill said.
A Russian operation put that playbook to work this week to spread a baseless accusation against a Democratic U.S. Senate candidate.

Linvill and several other research groups attributed them to Russian operators the research community has dubbed Storm-1516 . It's known for staging fake videos with actors and laundering their claims through influencer accounts with large followings.

Two fraudulent videos targeting the Senate candidate were posted on Tuesday on X by an account created last month that had few followers. The account's X profile said it was based in the U.S. but the social media platform publicly flagged it as possibly using a proxy such as a virtual private network, which could disguise its location.
OpenAI caught Russians and Iranians using ChatGPT for influence campaigns

The videos were likely created using artificial intelligence, according to Graphika, a research company that analyzes online communities. Linvill said a hallmark of Storm-1516 videos is the use of real actors whose faces are swapped using AI to look like someone else.

title_en: The 2028 crop hits New Mexico for inaugural ‘Matanza’ rally
title_zh: 2028 年作物登陆新墨西哥州，举办首届“Matanza”集会
summary: The “Fourth in the Nation Matanza Rally” is testing the appetite for a more Latino-specific cultural touchstone to round out the presidential candidate event rotation.
summary_zh: “全国第四届马坦萨集会”正在测试对更具拉丁裔特色的文化试金石的兴趣，以完善总统候选人
body_en: Prospective presidential candidates are known to chew over pork chops on a stick at Iowa’s iconic State Fair. They gather in South Carolina at Rep. Jim Clyburn’s “World Famous Fish Fry.” And they’re all over New Hampshire … well, any chance they get.
New Mexico today is entering the convening conversation with chicharrón at the “Matanza.”

In the long tradition of major state gatherings that have become dead giveaways of politicians’ presidential ambitions, New Mexico is formally stepping into the political fray, with an inaugural “Fourth in the Nation Matanza Rally” hosted by Democratic Sen. Ben Ray Luján designed to introduce the 2028 crop to the state.
What exactly is a Matanza? It’s a “New Mexico election season staple,” Deb Haaland, who was Interior secretary in the Biden administration and is running for New Mexico governor, told POLITICO.
“You dig a big hole in the ground, you build a fire, you put a pig in the coals, and it cooks overnight, and then you share this grand feast along with tortillas and chicharrón,” Haaland said.

Over 1,500 people, local and state leaders and New Mexico’s congressional delegation are gathering to eat and listen to mariachi and local bands at Albuquerque’s International Balloon Museum this afternoon, in part to rally voters to turn out on Nov. 3. Yet the presidential undertones are quite intentional in the new Democratic early nominating state.

“Matanzas typically in New Mexico have centered around family gatherings, weddings, big celebrations, community celebrations, bringing people together,” Luján told POLITICO. It’ll be a “first taste of New Mexico” for 2028ers to introduce themselves to the state.

New Mexico’s entry into the early nominating lineup has set a course for a primary season where some of the Democratic Party’s most elusive voters will be front and center. Some 2028ers will be hearing from voters directly today — among them Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.). Van Hollen has admitted he’s testing the waters for a presidential bid and told POLITICO “this is going to be part of that process.”
Also in the mix is Sen. Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.) — who wanted to be “neighborly” and show up for Luján — and said he’s “considering” a run but won’t make a decision until after the midterms.
“New Mexico is a lot like Arizona. We've got some shared issues and priorities,” Kelly told POLITICO. “And I think, you know, the Southwest is growing in importance, more people are moving here.”

But Luján is offering free advice for visiting Democrats: “Understand that you need to get out and earn the trust back from so many families where we lost support: labor families, union families, Hispanic families.”
Latino voters make up the majority of voters statewide, and together with Nevada they’re poised to dominate the early primary calendar.

“I think that both the fact that Trump betrayed voters when it came to the economy, plus the fact that they did a bait and switch when it came to their immigration policies, has turned off a lot of Hispanic voters,” Van Hollen told POLITICO. “But where Trump was right was recognizing people's economic pain.”
Blue collar work and agriculture run deep in the fabric of the state. “The [border] lines moved on a lot of families,” as Lujan put it — making the “New Mexican” identity particularly potent.

“We're the fifth-largest state in the country,” Haaland told POLITICO. “We have three national labs. We've got veteran services here. … We're also a border state, and so much commerce here in New Mexico happens on our border.”

And Haaland is also adamant about keeping Native Americans at the forefront of the 2028 conversation. “I want any presidential candidates to really know and understand why they need to think about tribes. Why they need to have a plan for Indian tribes when they're working on their platforms,” she said.

If Haaland wins the governorship, she and Luján will be critical touchpoints for 2028ers. Luján, a former DCCC chair, said he’s already started reaching out to potential candidates. And Haaland, through her gubernatorial campaign, has shared the stage with several of them already.

Pete Buttigieg hit the Land of Enchantment last month, campaigning for Haaland and Vasquez in the heavily Latino town of Las Cruces. Sen. Cory Booker (D-N.J.) held a fundraiser in the state in August. Michigan’s Gretchen Whitmer and Illinois’ JB Pritzker have both swung through the state. And Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham has been fielding calls from prospectives , including Rahm Emanuel and Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, who’s supporting Haaland as chair of the Democratic Governors Association.

But today marks the first official 2028 cattle call for the state. Complete with tribal leaders, local business owners and VIP donors, the first Matanza event will test the appetite for a more Latino-specific cultural touchstone that could round out the obligatory presidential candidate event rotation.
“What I hope that being fourth in the nation can create in New Mexico is a better understanding of what's needed across the West, across the Rocky Mountains, the high desert,” Luján told POLITICO.
body_zh: 众所周知，未来的总统候选人会在爱荷华州标志性的州博览会上咀嚼串在棍子上的猪排。他们聚集在南卡罗来纳州众议员吉姆·克莱伯恩的“世界著名炸鱼店”。他们遍布新罕布什尔州……好吧，他们一有机会就来。
新墨西哥州今天将在“马坦萨”与 chicharrón 进行会议。
重大州集会已成为政客总统野心的显露的长期传统，新墨西哥州正式介入政治争端，由民主党参议员本·雷·卢扬 (Ben Ray Luján) 主持的首届“全国第四届马坦萨集会”旨在向该州介绍 2028 年作物。
马坦萨到底是什么？曾担任拜登政府内政部长、正在竞选新墨西哥州州长的德布·哈兰 (Deb Haaland) 告诉《政治》杂志，这是“新墨西哥州选举季的主要内容”。
哈兰德说：“你在地上挖一个大洞，生火，把一头猪放进煤里，煮一夜，然后你就可以和玉米饼和辣椒一起分享这顿盛宴。”
今天下午，超过 1,500 人、地方和州领导人以及新墨西哥州国会代表团齐聚阿尔伯克基国际气球博物馆，一边吃饭一边听墨西哥流浪乐队和当地乐队的表演，部分原因是为了召集选民在 11 月 3 日投票。然而，在这个新的民主党提前提名州，总统的语气是有意为之的。
卢扬告诉《政治》杂志：“新墨西哥州的马坦萨斯活动通常以家庭聚会、婚礼、大型庆祝活动、社区庆祝活动以及将人们聚集在一起为中心。”对于 2028 年的人们来说，这将是“第一次品尝新墨西哥州”，向该州介绍自己。
新墨西哥州进入早期提名阵容已经为初选赛季奠定了基础，民主党中一些最难以捉摸的选民将成为焦点。一些 2028 支持者今天将直接听取选民的意见，其中包括参议员克里斯·范·霍伦（马里兰州民主党人）。范霍伦承认他正在试水总统竞选，并告诉《政治》杂志“这将是这一过程的一部分。”
参议员马克·凯利（亚利桑那州民主党人）也参与其中，他希望表现得“睦邻友好”并出席卢汉竞选，并表示他正在“考虑”参选，但要到中期选举后才会做出决定。
“新墨西哥州很像亚利桑那州。我们有一些共同的问题和优先事项，”凯利告诉《政治》杂志。 “我认为，你知道，西南部的重要性越来越大，越来越多的人搬到这里。”
但卢扬为来访的民主党人提供免费建议：“要明白，你需要走出去，赢得许多我们失去支持的家庭的信任：劳工家庭、工会家庭、西班牙裔家庭。”
拉丁裔选民占全州选民的大多数，他们与内华达州一起准备在早期初选日程中占据主导地位。
范霍伦告诉《政治》杂志：“我认为，特朗普在经济问题上背叛了选民，加上他们在移民政策上做了诱饵和改变，这已经让很多西班牙裔选民失去了兴趣。” “但特朗普的正确之处在于认识到人们的经济痛苦。”
蓝领工作和农业在该州根深蒂固。正如卢扬所说，“[边境]线对很多家庭产生了影响”——这使得“新墨西哥人”的身份变得特别有力。
“我们是该国第五大州，”哈兰德告诉《政治》杂志。 “我们有三个国家实验室。我们这里有退伍军人服务。……我们也是一个边境州，新墨西哥州的很多商业活动都发生在我们的边境上。”
哈兰德还坚持让美洲原住民处于 2028 年对话的最前沿。 “我希望任何总统候选人真正了解并理解为什么他们需要考虑部落。为什么他们在工作时需要为印第安部落制定一个计划，”她说。
如果哈兰德赢得州长职位，她和卢扬将成为 2028 人的关键接触点。 DCCC 前主席 Luján 表示，他已经开始接触潜在候选人。哈兰德通过她的州长竞选，已经与其中的几位同台了。

皮特·布蒂吉格上个月来到了“魔法之地”，在拉丁裔人口众多的拉斯克鲁塞斯小镇为哈兰德和瓦斯克斯竞选。新泽西州民主党参议员科里·布克 (Cory Booker) 八月在该州举办了一场筹款活动。密歇根州的格雷琴·惠特默(Gretchen Whitmer)和伊利诺伊州的JB·普利茨克(JB Pritzker)都曾在该州摇摆过。州长米歇尔·卢扬·格里沙姆一直在接听潜在候选人的电话，其中包括拉姆·伊曼纽尔和肯塔基州州长安迪·贝希尔，后者支持哈兰德担任民主党州长协会主席。
但今天标志着该州首次正式发出 2028 年牛的征集通知。首届马坦萨活动由部落领袖、当地企业主和 VIP 捐助者组成，将测试人们对更具拉丁裔特色的文化试金石的兴趣，从而完善总统候选人的强制性活动轮换。
“我希望成为全国第四名可以让新墨西哥州更好地了解西部地区、落基山脉和高原沙漠的需求，”卢扬告诉《政治》杂志。

title_en: The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows
title_zh: 报告显示，五角大楼的“负责任的人工智能”指导方针并不总是得到遵守
summary: The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with AI capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.
summary_zh: 五角大楼正在建造具有人工智能功能的武器和项目，官员们表示，这些项目并不总是严格遵守该机构自己的人工智能指导方针。
body_en: The Pentagon’s guidelines for “responsible AI” aren’t always followed, report shows : NPR
Podcasts & Shows Expand/collapse submenu for Podcasts & Shows

The Pentagon’s guidelines for “responsible AI” aren’t always followed, report shows The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with AI capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.
The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows
Three of the Pentagon projects surveyed by GAO included weapons for counter-camouflage (upper image) and target recognition (lower images). Government Accountability Office/GAO hide caption

The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with artificial intelligence capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.

AI researchers and international organizations have long advocated for strict regulation of AI when used in weapons that could become unpredictable or function with little human control, arguing that those tools could endanger the lives of soldiers and civilians and risk quickly escalating wars. But Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has repeatedly dismissed previous caution of AI tools and encouraged rapid autonomous innovation at the Pentagon.

The Pentagon issued a memo in January saying the department would become "an 'AI-first' warfighting force across all components, from front to back." Last month, Hegseth announced a new warfare command focused on autonomous weapon development, including drones.
Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth arrives on stage for a discussion during an annual Army meeting on October 14, 2026 in Washington, DC. Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images North America hide caption
The watchdog report, published by the U.S. Government Accountability Office on Oct. 14, grants a rare look inside how those kinds of projects are being developed.

The GAO surveyed 10 officials involved with building 10 weapons and tools for the Pentagon that use AI to automatically identify targets on the battlefield, process surveillance and improve tactical decision making, and other tasks. The projects are among more than 300 being built with AI in the Pentagon.
When responding to the GAO survey, six of the 10 officials said their teams had "identified risk(s)" with using the projects "in an operational environment."

To address some of those sorts of risks, in 2021, the Pentagon sent a memo outlining six basic tenets to ensure that weapons built with AI are created responsibly. Those six guidelines mainly stress the importance of Pentagon-wide oversight, verification and "real-time monitoring" of the technology, and cooperation with allies "to advance global norms grounded in shared values."

Alissa Czyz, who directed the GAO review, said the tenets evolved from earlier ethical principles, and while they weren't rules, they were understood to be important by people involved with building AI tools at the Pentagon.
"It's a memo, right, at the end of the day, so it's not a department instruction," said Czyz. "It's something that the department has signaled that should be implemented."

Most of the people involved with making the 10 weapons and projects reviewed by GAO had taken "at least initial steps" to follow the six tenets outlined in the memo, according to the report, and some of the projects were in early stages, Czyz clarified.
But some of the responses indicated officials weren't always closely following the guidelines.

Four officials told the GAO that requirements for the weapons and projects they were working on weren't "aligned with Responsible AI tenets." And three of the 10 officials told the GAO they "don't know" if the projects will be continuously monitored after they're deployed, though the six tenets encourage monitoring.
Hegseth speech leans on culture war flashpoints

Officials told the GAO that more access to expertise about the agency's guidelines or staff who know about them would increase their ability to incorporate AI responsibly. But the group that helps manage education on the Pentagon's guidelines, the Department of the Responsible AI Division, is understaffed. Although the group was authorized to hire 10 people in 2023, as of February, only three of those positions were filled and the Pentagon "is unlikely to fill vacant positions or increase staffing," the report states.

2026 年 10 月 14 日在华盛顿特区举行的陆军年度会议上，国防部长皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth) 登上讲台进行讨论。凯文迪奇/盖蒂图片社北美隐藏标题栏
美国政府问责办公室 10 月 14 日发布的这份监管报告罕见地揭示了此类项目的开发情况。
美国政府问责局对参与为五角大楼制造 10 种武器和工具的 10 名官员进行了调查，这些武器和工具使用人工智能自动识别战场上的目标、处理监视和改进战术决策以及其他任务。这些项目是五角大楼利用人工智能建造的 300 多个项目之一。
在回应 GAO 调查时，10 名官员中有 6 名表示，他们的团队已“识别出”在“运营环境”中使用这些项目的风险。
为了解决其中一些风险，五角大楼在 2021 年发送了一份备忘录，概述了六项基本原则，以确保以负责任的方式制造人工智能制造的武器。这六项指导方针主要强调五角大楼范围内对该技术进行监督、验证和“实时监控”以及与盟友合作“以推进基于共同价值观的全球规范”的重要性。
负责 GAO 审查的 Alissa Czyz 表示，这些原则是从早期的道德原则演变而来的，虽然它们不是规则，但五角大楼参与构建人工智能工具的人员认为它们很重要。
“这只是一份备忘录，对吧，归根结底，所以它不是部门指令，”齐兹说。 “该部门已表示应该实施这一举措。”
报告称，大多数参与政府问责局审查的 10 种武器和项目制造的人员都采取了“至少初步步骤”来遵循备忘录中概述的六项原则，其中一些项目还处于早期阶段，Czyz 澄清道。
但一些回应表明，官员们并不总是严格遵守这些指导方针。
四名官员告诉政府问责局，他们正在研究的武器和项目的要求“不符合负责任的人工智能原则”。 10 名官员中的 3 名告诉政府问责局，他们“不知道”这些项目在部署后是否会受到持续监控，尽管六项原则鼓励监控。
赫格赛斯的演讲侧重于文化战争的爆发点
官员们告诉政府问责局，更多地获得有关该机构指南的专业知识或了解这些指南的工作人员将提高他们负责任地整合人工智能的能力。但帮助管理五角大楼指导方针教育的小组——负责任的人工智能部门——人手不足。报告称，尽管该组织被授权在 2023 年雇用 10 名员工，但截至 2 月份，其中只有 3 个职位被填补，五角大楼“不太可能填补空缺职位或增加人员配置”。

Ohio’s rural voters key in state’s competitive Senate race Ohio has been a reliably red state for several elections but it's competitive this year. If Democrats want to prevail, they'll have to win people who have backed Republicans, like rural voters.
Ohio could decide control of the Senate. Its rural voters might decide the winner
Chris Gibbs, a cattle farmer in rural Ohio, says he's been in a deficit for almost three years. Keren Carrión/NPR hide caption

At the weekday farmers market in Athens, Ohio, colorful vegetables are on display for patrons to purchase, community members interact with each other and vendors and one another. It feels like most people in attendance know one another on some personal level.
For a small town like Athens, the farmers market is a gathering place.
"Our Saturday markets have been fully at capacity," said Paige Walters, the Athens farmers market promotions manager.
Athens, Ohio is home to Ohio University. The city is, like many college towns, pretty liberal. But that's not the case in most of the Appalachian communities in the region.
Walters noticed that this year, for the first time in a while, the Athens County Republican Party has set up a table at the market.
"I think that does speak to the political climate right now – that it's pretty competitive," she said.

Despite its past as a swing state, Ohio is now considered to be reliably Republican. This election is a little different. With toss-up races for governor and U.S. Senate, Democrats have a chance to win statewide.
But if Democrats want to win, they have to capture voters who voted for Republicans in the past. That includes the rural Ohio voter base, which historically leans conservative.

While rural voters nationwide have voted red in the past (they backed Trump in 2024 by 40 points), recent polling has shown his approval rating in rural America dropping dramatically amid high inflation, tariffs and the war in Iran.

Democrats are trying to gain ground in the unexpected areas. That's especially true in the competitive Senate match up between Sen. Jon Husted, the Republican nominee, and former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown as both candidates invest in outreach to rural parts of the state.
"There's a lot of people in rural Ohio that are not happy, whether it's gas prices, diesel prices, the tariffs, the war," Matthew White of Athens told NPR at the farmers market.
Multicolored bell peppers, onions and squash line the table at the Cowdery Farms booth. While the weekday market usually has slower foot traffic, farmer Larry Cowdery sold a good amount of produce.
He owns a small vegetable farm along the Ohio River in Long Bottom. There are two big concerns at the top of Cowdrey's mind. The first is the cost of healthcare.
"The big, big issue that we run into is since we're self-employed, we have to find health insurance somewhere," he told NPR. "It's going to be much more expensive next year."

Healthcare premiums on the Affordable Care Act marketplace are expected to increase by roughly 15% in Ohio , in part because of the expiration of federal subsidies. Republicans, including Husted, voted to eliminate the subsidies under the Trump-backed "One Big Beautiful Bill." As a result of sticker shock, Ohio saw the biggest drop — tied with Oklahoma for the most in the nation — in the number of people enrolled in the marketplace last year, with a nearly 33% decline in enrollment.

俄亥俄州可以决定参议院的控制权。农村选民可能会决定获胜者
俄亥俄州农村地区的养牛户克里斯·吉布斯 (Chris Gibbs) 表示，他已经陷入赤字近三年了。 Keren Carrión/NPR 隐藏标题栏
在俄亥俄州雅典市的平日农贸市场上，展示着色彩缤纷的蔬菜供顾客购买，社区成员之间以及商贩之间相互互动。感觉大多数出席的人在某种个人层面上都互相认识。
对于雅典这样的小镇来说，农贸市场是一个聚集地。
“我们周六的市场已经满员了，”雅典农贸市场促销经理佩奇·沃尔特斯 (Paige Walters) 说。
俄亥俄州雅典市是俄亥俄大学的所在地。和许多大学城一样，这座城市相当自由。但该地区大多数阿巴拉契亚社区的情况并非如此。
沃尔特斯注意到，今年，雅典县共和党一段时间以来第一次在市场上摆起了桌子。
“我认为这确实反映了现在的政治气候——竞争相当激烈，”她说。
尽管俄亥俄州过去是一个摇摆州，但现在被认为是可靠的共和党州。这次选举有点不同。在州长和美国参议院的角逐中，民主党有机会赢得全州选举。
但如果民主党想获胜，他们就必须赢得过去投票给共和党的选民。其中包括历史上倾向保守的俄亥俄州农村选民基础。
虽然全国农村选民过去都投了红色票（他们在 2024 年以 40 个百分点的支持率支持特朗普），但最近的民意调查显示，由于高通胀、关税和伊朗战争，他在美国农村地区的支持率急剧下降。
民主党正试图在意想不到的领域取得进展。在共和党候选人参议员乔恩·赫斯特德和前民主党参议员谢罗德·布朗之间的参议院竞争中尤其如此，因为两位候选人都投资于对该州农村地区的推广。
“俄亥俄州农村地区有很多人不满意，无论是汽油价格、柴油价格、关税还是战争，”雅典的马修·怀特在农贸市场告诉美国国家公共广播电台。
Cowdery Farms 摊位的桌子上摆满了五彩缤纷的甜椒、洋葱和南瓜。虽然工作日市场的人流量通常较慢，但农民拉里·考德里却售出了大量农产品。
他在俄亥俄河沿岸的朗博顿拥有一个小型蔬菜农场。考德雷最关心的问题有两个。首先是医疗保健费用。
“我们遇到的一个非常非常大的问题是，由于我们是个体经营者，我们必须在某个地方找到健康保险，”他告诉 NPR。 “明年的价格会贵得多。”
俄亥俄州《平价医疗法案》市场的医疗保费预计将增加约 15%，部分原因是联邦补贴到期。包括赫斯特德在内的共和党人投票决定取消特朗普支持的“一项美丽的大法案”下的补贴。由于价格冲击，俄亥俄州去年的市场注册人数下降幅度最大，与俄克拉荷马州并列全国降幅最大的州，注册人数下降了近 33%。

Trump’s East Potomac vision alarms D.C. runners, cyclists, birders Trump's most recent rendering of East Potomac Park overtakes the D.C. peninsula with a sprawling golf course, without the grassy areas and road beloved by locals. That's prompted grassroots pushback.
A D.C. park was made 'for the pleasure of the people.' Trump's plan would change that
East Potomac overhaul would disrupt more than golf
Embed iframe src="https://www.npr.org/player/embed/nx-s1-6010488/nx-s1-9976734" width="100%" height="290" frameborder="0" scrolling="no" title="NPR embedded audio player">

Locals rally against Trump's potential redevelopment of East Potomac Park at a protest in early October. Runners, cyclists, birders and more worry they will lose access to the park under Trump's plan to overhaul the municipal golf course. Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

WASHINGTON, D.C. — President Trump's express wish to take over the East Potomac Golf Links has thrust a municipal D.C. golf course into the national spotlight. But locals rely on that area for much more than golfing — and worry the district could lose an invaluable recreational oasis.

The southern tip of East Potomac Park, known as Hains Point, is beloved by cyclists, runners, picnickers and birders for its waterfront views, cherry trees and Ohio Drive, the scenic three-mile loop around its perimeter. Runners use the wide, flat road to train; it's even a fixture of several major race courses, including the Marine Corps Marathon on Sunday.
Judge chastises Trump administration plan to push ahead overhaul of DC golf course

"It's such an important part of the fabric of this region, even though it's not very well known [beyond it]," said Elizabeth Kiker, the executive director of the Washington Area Bicyclists Association. She herself took her now-husband on a bike ride on their second date 20 years ago.

Locals describe Hains Point as a rare public resource in D.C. It's easily accessible from the National Mall yet removed from the crowds, full of people but free of traffic. Congress created it in 1897 , "to be forever held and used as a park for the recreation and pleasure of the people."
And yet, under the president's proposed golf course redesign, Hains Point as people know and love it may cease to exist.
East Potomac Golf Links and Hains Point as seen from the top of the Washington Monument this week. Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

Trump said on Truth Social last weekend that renovations would keep the entire park closed for 15 months starting in November. But it's not clear what would be left when it reopens: The rendering he posted shows an 18-hole course spanning the entire peninsula — including the current playground and picnic area on its southern tip — with no road visible around the perimeter.

The White House referred NPR to the Department of the Interior, which did not respond to NPR's questions about whether those features would be removed as part of the redesign. The proposed renovations have so far been the subject of mixed messages from the administration: Trump said last weekend that work would begin in mid-November, then "immediately." But government lawyers said in court Monday that they were not aware of a final plan .

Even so, the government abruptly downed hundreds of trees on the course with little warning earlier this month, which critics worry was a pretext for beginning renovations. (The government says it was following up on recommendations from a 2019 landscaping report.) Judge Ana Reyes held a hearing on Monday to learn more about the tree-clearing and decide whether to block further work on the golf course.

But it's not just the golf course that's at stake, as a group called Hains Point Runners told Reyes in the courtroom and a written brief. In its 35-page brief, the group says federal law requires the National Park Service to identify and consider the "longstanding recreational uses of the Hains Point corridor" and ways to avoid harming those uses, before embarking on any work that would change it.
Judge grills government lawyers over Trump's plan to renovate a DC golf course
"From the perspective of the running community, that did not occur here," lawyers wrote.

特朗普对东波托马克公园的愿景让华盛顿特区的跑步者、骑自行车者和观鸟者感到震惊。特朗普最近对东波托马克公园的描绘超越了华盛顿半岛，拥有一个庞大的高尔夫球场，没有当地人喜爱的草地和道路。这引起了草根阶层的抵制。
华盛顿公园是“为了人民的欢乐”而建造的。特朗普的计划将改变这一现状
东波托马克大修将扰乱的不仅仅是高尔夫
嵌入iframe src =“https://www.npr.org/player/embed/nx-s1-6010488/nx-s1-9976734”宽度=“100％”高度=“290”frameborder =“0”滚动=“否”标题=“NPR嵌入式音频播放器”>
十月初，当地人举行抗议活动，反对特朗普可能重建东波托马克公园的计划。跑步者、骑自行车者、观鸟者等人担心，根据特朗普整顿市政高尔夫球场的计划，他们将无法进入公园。索尔·勒布/法新社通过盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
华盛顿特区——特朗普总统明确表示希望接管东波托马克高尔夫球场，这使得华盛顿特区的一座市政高尔夫球场成为全国关注的焦点。但当地人对这个地区的依赖远不止打高尔夫球，他们担心该地区可能会失去宝贵的休闲绿洲。
东波托马克公园的南端被称为海恩斯角 (Hains Point)，因其海滨景观、樱桃树和俄亥俄大道 (Ohio Drive)（环绕其周边的三英里环线风景优美）而深受骑自行车者、跑步者、野餐者和观鸟者的喜爱。跑步者使用宽阔平坦的道路进行训练；它甚至是几个主要赛场的固定项目，包括周日的海军陆战队马拉松比赛。
法官严厉谴责特朗普政府推动华盛顿特区高尔夫球场检修的计划
华盛顿地区自行车协会执行董事伊丽莎白·基克 (Elizabeth Kiker) 表示：“它是该地区结构的重要组成部分，尽管它[除此之外]并不为人所知。” 20 年前，她第二次约会时，她亲自带着现在的丈夫骑自行车。
当地人将海恩斯角描述为华盛顿特区难得的公共资源。从国家广场可以轻松到达这里，但又远离人群，挤满了人，但没有交通拥堵。国会于 1897 年创建了它，“永久保留并用作人民休闲娱乐的公园”。
然而，根据总统提议的高尔夫球场重新设计，人们所熟知和喜爱的海恩斯角可能不复存在。
本周从华盛顿纪念碑顶部看到的东波托马克高尔夫球场和海恩斯角。索尔·勒布/法新社通过盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
特朗普上周末在Truth Social上表示，整修工程将使整个公园从11月开始关闭15个月。但目前尚不清楚重新开放后会留下什么：他发布的效果图显示了一个横跨整个半岛的 18 洞球场，包括目前的游乐场和南端的野餐区，周边看不到任何道路。
白宫将 NPR 转介给内政部，但内政部没有回应 NPR 关于这些功能是否会作为重新设计的一部分被删除的问题。迄今为止，拟议的翻修工程一直是政府发出的混杂信息的主题：特朗普上周末表示，工程将于 11 月中旬开始，然后“立即”开始。但政府律师周一在法庭上表示，他们不知道最终计划。
即便如此，本月早些时候，政府在没有任何警告的情况下突然砍倒了球场上的数百棵树，批评者担心这是开始整修的借口。 （政府表示正在跟进 2019 年景观美化报告中的建议。）法官安娜·雷耶斯 (Ana Reyes) 周一举行了听证会，了解有关树木清理的更多信息，并决定是否阻止高尔夫球场的进一步施工。
但正如一个名为 Hains Point Runners 的组织在法庭上和一份书面陈述中告诉雷耶斯的那样，受到威胁的不仅仅是高尔夫球场。该组织在长达 35 页的简报中表示，联邦法律要求国家公园管理局在开展任何可能改变这些用途的工作之前，必须确定并考虑“海恩斯角走廊的长期娱乐用途”以及避免损害这些用途的方法。
法官就特朗普翻新华盛顿高尔夫球场的计划盘问政府律师
“从跑步界的角度来看，这种情况并没有发生在这里，”律师写道。

title_en: As Israeli election looms, Trump advisers see opportunity beyond Netanyahu
title_zh: 随着以色列大选临近，特朗普顾问看到了内塔尼亚胡以外的机会
summary: President Trump has endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu in Tuesday's Israeli election, but some of his advisers see opportunity for his Middle East agenda in a government led by someone else, U.S. officials tell Axios. Why it matters: Trump has never worked with an Is
summary_zh: 特朗普总统在周二的以色列选举中支持本杰明·内塔尼亚胡，但他的一些顾问认为他的中东议程有机会
body_en: President Trump has endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu in Tuesday's Israeli election, but some of his advisers see opportunity for his Middle East agenda in a government led by someone else, U.S. officials tell Axios.

Why it matters: Trump has never worked with an Israeli prime minister other than Netanyahu, and doesn't personally know any of the other candidates. The two have forged a close but often turbulent relationship.
"He's the devil he knows," one Trump adviser said, describing the president's view of Netanyahu.

Driving the news: After weeks of hesitation, Trump endorsed Netanyahu on Sunday — and even suggested his defeat would have consequences for U.S.-Israel relations. One U.S. official described the endorsement as a win-win for Trump, regardless of the outcome.
If Netanyahu wins — or remains in power as caretaker prime minister — Trump could claim credit for rescuing him politically and use that leverage to press for concessions.

If Netanyahu loses and his opponents form a government, Israel's new leaders would still have every incentive to cultivate good relations with Trump. His endorsement of their rival would quickly become a footnote.

Behind the scenes: Many of Trump's closest advisers opposed his decision to endorse Netanyahu, believing the president should stay out of the Israeli election, according to sources familiar with the discussions.
Vice President Vance notably declined to follow Trump's lead when asked about the election this week, amid growing hostility toward Netanyahu in parts of the MAGA movement.
"I'm not attacking Bibi Netanyahu. I'm not endorsing Bibi Netanyahu. I think the president's endorsement is ultimately what matters," Vance told reporters.
Zoom in: Vance, who endorsed former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán days before his election defeat in April , said he would no longer get involved in foreign elections.
The vice president is among the senior Trump officials who became disillusioned with Netanyahu during the war with Iran, according to sources familiar with their thinking.

Vance and other top aides believe Netanyahu's pre-war assessments to the White House were mistaken, deepening questions about whether he remains the best partner for achieving Trump's regional ambitions.

The big picture: Once the Israeli election and U.S. midterms are over, Trump will face a defining choice for his Middle East agenda: whether to join Netanyahu in another major military operation against Iran.
Netanyahu is eager to move forward. But the election results could influence Trump's decision, or at least the timing of any renewed large-scale fighting.

Trump also wants to move beyond the Iran war and pursue an ambitious diplomatic agenda that includes implementing his Gaza peace plan , brokering deals between Israel and Lebanon and Syria , and ultimately securing a historic Israeli-Saudi peace agreement .
Whether Trump can make progress on those goals will depend in part on who governs Israel — and what kind of coalition emerges from Tuesday's vote.
The intrigue: Behind the scenes over the last six months, several of Trump's top advisers have grown dissatisfied with Netanyahu on key regional priorities.
Gaza: Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have expressed frustration with Netanyahu's reluctance to advance implementation of the president's peace plan.
Syria: Trump's envoy Tom Barrack has similar concerns about the Netanyahu government's approach to Damascus and continued Israeli military operations in Syria.

Lebanon and the West Bank: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his team have a better relationship with Netanyahu, but believe Israel could do more to strengthen Lebanon's government. They are also frustrated by Netanyahu's failure to do more to curb settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank.
body_zh: 美国官员告诉 Axios，特朗普总统在周二的以色列选举中支持了本杰明·内塔尼亚胡，但他的一些顾问认为，在由其他人领导的政府中，他的中东议程有机会实现。
为什么重要：除了内塔尼亚胡之外，特朗普从未与以色列总理合作过，而且他个人也不认识任何其他候选人。两人建立了密切但经常动荡的关系。
“他是他所认识的魔鬼，”特朗普的一位顾问在描述总统对内塔尼亚胡的看法时说道。
推动这一消息的是：经过数周的犹豫后，特朗普周日支持了内塔尼亚胡，甚至暗示他的失败将对美以关系产生影响。一位美国官员称，无论结果如何，这一支持对特朗普来说都是双赢。
如果内塔尼亚胡获胜——或者继续担任看守总理——特朗普可以声称自己在政治上拯救了他，并利用这一影响力迫使他让步。
如果内塔尼亚胡失败并且他的对手组建政府，以色列新领导人仍然有充分的动力与特朗普建立良好关系。他对对手的支持很快就成为一个脚注。
幕后：据熟悉讨论的消息人士透露，特朗普的许多最亲密的顾问反对他支持内塔尼亚胡的决定，认为总统应该远离以色列选举。
由于 MAGA 运动部分地区对内塔尼亚胡的敌意与日俱增，副总统万斯在被问及本周的选举时明显拒绝追随特朗普的领导。
“我不是在攻击比比·内塔尼亚胡。我不是在支持比比·内塔尼亚胡。我认为总统的支持最终才是最重要的，”万斯告诉记者。
放大：万斯在四月份选举失败前几天支持匈牙利前总理欧尔班维克托，他表示将不再参与外国选举。
据知情人士透露，副总统是在与伊朗的战争期间对内塔尼亚胡失望的特朗普高级官员之一。
万斯和其他高级助手认为内塔尼亚胡战前对白宫的评估是错误的，这加深了人们对他是否仍然是实现特朗普地区野心的最佳合作伙伴的疑问。
大局：一旦以色列大选和美国中期选举结束，特朗普的中东议程将面临一个决定性的选择：是否与内塔尼亚胡一起对伊朗发动另一场重大军事行动。
内塔尼亚胡渴望向前迈进。但选举结果可能会影响特朗普的决定，或者至少影响重新爆发大规模战斗的时间。
特朗普还希望超越伊朗战争，推行雄心勃勃的外交议程，包括实施他的加沙和平计划，促成以色列与黎巴嫩和叙利亚之间的协议，并最终达成历史性的以色列-沙特和平协议。
特朗普能否在这些目标上取得进展将部分取决于谁来统治以色列，以及周二的投票会产生什么样的联盟。
阴谋：在过去六个月的幕后，特朗普的几位高级顾问对内塔尼亚胡在关键地区优先事项上越来越不满。
加沙：特朗普的特使史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳对内塔尼亚胡不愿推进总统和平计划的实施表示失望。
叙利亚：特朗普的特使汤姆·巴拉克对内塔尼亚胡政府对大马士革的态度以及以色列在叙利亚持续的军事行动也有类似的担忧。
黎巴嫩和约旦河西岸：国务卿马可·卢比奥及其团队与内塔尼亚胡关系更好，但相信以色列可以采取更多措施来加强黎巴嫩政府。他们还对内塔尼亚胡未能采取更多措施遏制定居者对西岸巴勒斯坦人的袭击感到沮丧。

body_en: Additional 178 cases of measles reported by US health authorities amid outbreak | US healthcare | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation
Additional 178 cases of measles reported by US health authorities amid outbreak
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 4,588 cases across the country, more than double the tally in 2025
Federal health authorities reported an additional 178 cases of measles in the US this week, as the vaccine-preventable illness continues to sicken people across at least 43 outbreaks.

The new data reported by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) comes as experts criticize the agency for lack of transparency, and as health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr takes steps to further upend US vaccine infrastructure.

The CDC reported 4,588 cases of measles across the country in 2026 as of Friday – more than double the tally for 2025. Pennsylvania alone reported 1,338 cases on the same day. The CDC also reported large outbreaks in South Carolina and Utah, both of which are reporting more than 500 cases.
CDC denies approval for high-volume measles test, citing ‘other priorities’

In spite of rising measles numbers, official tallies represent an undercount of the disease. Measles is widely regarded as one of the most contagious diseases known to medicine. Its most common symptoms – rash, runny nose, fever and cough – may not immediately send the infected to a doctor.

Measles sends one in five unvaccinated people who become infected to the hospital, and one to three people in 1,000 die of disease-related complications. The measles vaccine is 97% effective at preventing the disease. Vaccine side effects include injection-site soreness and low-grade fever. The measles vaccine has been a focal point of anti-vaccine activism for decades.

In Pennsylvania, which has had the worst outbreak in the nation for months, state authorities have reported five measles-associated deaths and are investigating a sixth. The CDC has reported three measles deaths nationally, but has refused to say where the third death took place, obscuring whether it is counting a death in Pennsylvania or elsewhere.
Kennedy reportedly asked senior CDC officials in September to remove a measles death from the official tally after he questioned whether the disease contributed to the death, according to Reuters .

In addition to criticism of how the CDC has tallied measles deaths, Health and Human Services (HHS) this week announced changes to vaccine injury reporting systems. A proposal will allow doctors to bill for reporting suspected vaccine injuries, among other changes.

The “vaccine adverse event reporting system”, or VAERS, has been a long-time fixation of the anti-vaccine movement. The system has proved useful for researchers tracking rare vaccine safety issues. However, it has also become a source of misinformation for anti-vaccine activists, who point to VAERS to make claims, however unfounded, about safety.

All vaccines have risks – a fact acknowledged by vaccinologists . Before Kennedy’s appointment to the health department, an expert panel considered each vaccine change individually to decide whether benefits outweigh risks. Kennedy fired all 17 sitting members of that board. He replaced them with members with whom he ideologically aligned. A court blocked the members’ appointment in March.

In his time as secretary, Kennedy also misleadingly claimed children get more than 90 vaccine doses ; linked vaccines to autism in spite of extensive evidence to the contrary; directed the CDC to remove claims that vaccines do not cause autism from its website; claimed the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine contains “ aborted fetal debris ”; and stated that vitamin A and cod liver oil may help children with measles, which leading physicians described as misleading.

美国卫生当局报告麻疹疫情期间新增 178 例麻疹病例
美国疾病控制与预防中心报告全国有 4,588 例病例，是 2025 年病例数的两倍多
联邦卫生当局本周报告美国新增 178 例麻疹病例，这种疫苗可预防的疾病在至少 43 次疫情中继续使人们患病。
美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 报告新数据之际，专家批评该机构缺乏透明度，而卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪 (Robert F Kennedy Jr) 则采取措施进一步颠覆美国疫苗基础设施。
截至周五，美国疾病控制和预防中心 (CDC) 报告称，2026 年全国有 4,588 例麻疹病例，是 2025 年病例数的两倍多。仅宾夕法尼亚州当天就报告了 1,338 例麻疹病例。 CDC 还报告了南卡罗来纳州和犹他州的大规模疫情爆发，这两个州均报告了 500 多例病例。
疾病预防控制中心以“其他优先事项”为由，拒绝批准大规模麻疹检测
尽管麻疹人数不断上升，但官方统计数字仍低估了这种疾病。麻疹被广泛认为是医学上已知的最具传染性的疾病之一。它最常见的症状——皮疹、流鼻涕、发烧和咳嗽——可能不会立即将感染者送去看医生。
麻疹导致五分之一未接种疫苗的感染者被送往医院，千分之一到三人死于与疾病相关的并发症。麻疹疫苗预防该疾病的有效率为 97%。疫苗副作用包括注射部位疼痛和低烧。几十年来，麻疹疫苗一直是反疫苗运动的焦点。
在宾夕法尼亚州，几个月来该州疫情最为严重，该州当局报告了五例与麻疹相关的死亡事件，并正在调查第六例。疾病预防控制中心报告了全国三例麻疹死亡病例，但拒绝透露第三例死亡病例发生在哪里，从而模糊了它是否在统计宾夕法尼亚州或其他地方的死亡病例。
据路透社报道，肯尼迪在质疑麻疹是否导致死亡后，于 9 月份要求疾病预防控制中心高级官员将麻疹死亡人数从官方统计中删除。
除了对疾病预防控制中心统计麻疹死亡人数的批评之外，卫生与公众服务部 (HHS) 本周还宣布对疫苗伤害报告系统进行更改。除其他变化外，一项提案将允许医生对报告疑似疫苗伤害进行收费。
“疫苗不良事件报告系统”（VAERS）长期以来一直是反疫苗运动的固定内容。事实证明，该系统对于研究人员追踪罕见的疫苗安全问题很有用。然而，它也成为反疫苗活动人士错误信息的来源，他们指出 VAERS 是关于安全性的说法，尽管毫无根据。
所有疫苗都有风险——这是疫苗学家承认的事实。在肯尼迪被任命为卫生部门之前，一个专家小组单独考虑了每种疫苗的变化，以决定益处是否大于风险。肯尼迪解雇了该委员会的全部 17 名现任成员。他用与他在意识形态上一致的成员取代了他们。法院于三月份阻止了这些成员的任命。
肯尼迪在担任国务卿期间还误导性地声称儿童接种了超过 90 剂疫苗；尽管有大量相反的证据，但仍将疫苗与自闭症联系起来；指示疾病预防控制中心从其网站上删除有关疫苗不会导致自闭症的声明；声称麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹疫苗含有“流产胎儿碎片”；并指出维生素 A 和鱼肝油可能有助于治疗麻疹儿童，但主流医生认为这是一种误导。

body_en: Epstein files take back seat in midterms but experts say issue has not gone away | US politics | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation
Epstein files take back seat in midterms but experts say issue has not gone away
Other voter concerns have prevailed but return of Congress likely to see renewed focus on late sex offender’s activities

As US voters head to the polls for crucial and fraught midterm elections, some survivors’ advocates in the Jeffrey Epstein investigation have expressed concern that the scandal could recede into the background.

Political experts believe, however, the Epstein issue is not going away permanently and that many voters can balance day-to-day concerns such as affordability and AI with the scandal involving the late financier and accused sex trafficker whose social circle was widespread among America’s elite.

“My greatest concern is not that the public will forget Jeffrey Epstein, but that the politicians and institutions responsible for accountability will use the chaos of world events as an excuse to move on,” said Spencer Kuvin of Goldlaw, who has represented multiple Epstein survivors.

Kuvin added: “Wars, economic crises and political controversies may dominate the headlines, but they do not erase the suffering of the victims or the unanswered questions about how Epstein and his powerful associates were allowed to operate for decades.

“Justice should not have an expiration date, and it certainly should not be dictated by the news cycle. We cannot allow the Epstein scandal to become yesterday’s news simply because today’s headlines are more urgent.”
Epstein’s attorney and accountant accused of ‘facilitating and concealing’ his crimes in lawsuit
Kuvin called for the US government to continue releasing Epstein files – which many have said were excluded from allegedly incomplete disclosures – and for Congress to demand accountability.

“It has been disappointing to have seen attention diverted from Jeffrey Epstein in the past year,” said Jennifer Freeman of Marsh Law, who represents numerous Epstein survivors in litigation surrounding his sexual abuse of teenage girls.

Freeman, however, expressed optimism about the long-term prospects of justice for survivors, saying: “While public attention may have shifted from the Epstein case, given the electoral cycle, I am confident it will command concentration and accountability shortly again.”

Freeman noted that she was continuing to pursue a lawsuit against the US government for alleged negligence “in repeatedly, for decades, dropping the ball on investigating and prosecuting Epstein”. She is also litigating a class-action lawsuit against his estate related to his collection and production of child sex abuse images.
Political experts said that Epstein might get less attention from campaigning politicians and voters, but that it was probably a temporary dip, not a permanent drop-off.

“It really does feel like everything is on fire. I think people can care about several things at once, but what’s directly affecting their lives tends to take priority,” Brittany Martinez, a Republican strategist who works as acting director of Principles First, said. “When they’re worried about gas prices, living costs and whether their government is working for them, that can push Epstein out of the immediate conversation.

“I don’t think the questions or the demand for answers have gone away; they’re just competing for attention. So I’d expect to hear less about it for stretches, rather than see it disappear altogether.”
“There’s just something every day with Trump,” said Shawn Donahue, clinical associate professor in the University at Buffalo’s department of political science.

For Donahue, timing also plays a key role. The US Congress has been in recess and without members on the House floor, so there’s not any discussion of the Epstein Files Transparency Act’s proposed new iteration. This bill, the Epstein Files Transparency Act II , seeks to address what advocates have said are shortfalls in the present EFTA – such as an absence of enforcement mechanisms.

“It kind of feels like whenever Congress comes back into session, this probably starts to become more of an issue again, and especially if Democrats are looking at being in control of one or maybe both chambers of Congress,” Donahue said.
Should Democrats win the house, as polls project, Donahue expects they will swiftly “put Republicans on the spot” with Epstein. “Democrats are ready to start on the investigation from day one.”

爱泼斯坦文件在中期选举中退居二线，但专家表示问题并未消失
其他选民的担忧也占了上风，但国会回归后可能会重新关注已故性犯罪者的活动
随着美国选民前往投票站参加至关重要且令人担忧的中期选举，杰弗里·爱泼斯坦调查中的一些幸存者的支持者表示担心这起丑闻可能会退居幕后。
然而，政治专家认为，爱泼斯坦问题不会永远消失，许多选民可以在负担能力和人工智能等日常担忧与涉及已故金融家和被指控的性贩运者的丑闻之间取得平衡，后者的社交圈在美国精英中广泛存在。
“我最担心的不是公众会忘记杰弗里·爱泼斯坦，而是负责问责的政客和机构会利用世界事件的混乱作为继续前进的借口，”代表多位爱泼斯坦幸存者的戈德劳公司的斯宾塞·库文说。
库文补充道：“战争、经济危机和政治争议可能占据头条新闻，但它们并不能消除受害者的痛苦，也不能消除有关爱泼斯坦及其强大同伙数十年来如何被允许运作的悬而未决的问题。
“正义不应该有有效期，它当然不应该由新闻周期决定。我们不能仅仅因为今天的头条新闻更紧急，就让爱泼斯坦丑闻成为昨天的新闻。”
爱泼斯坦的律师和会计师被指控在诉讼中“协助和隐瞒”他的罪行
库文呼吁美国政府继续公布爱泼斯坦的文件——许多人称这些文件被排除在所谓的不完整披露之外——并要求国会要求问责。
马什律师事务所 (Marsh Law) 的詹妮弗·弗里曼 (Jennifer Freeman) 表示：“过去一年，人们的注意力从杰弗里·爱泼斯坦身上转移，这令人失望。”她在有关爱泼斯坦性虐待少女的诉讼中代表众多爱泼斯坦幸存者。
然而，弗里曼对幸存者伸张正义的长期前景表示乐观，他说：“虽然公众的注意力可能已经从爱泼斯坦案件上转移，但考虑到选举周期，我相信很快就会再次集中注意力并承担责任。”
弗里曼指出，她正在继续对美国政府提起诉讼，指控其“数十年来在调查和起诉爱泼斯坦方面一再失败”。她还在对他的遗产提起集体诉讼，该诉讼涉及他收集和制作儿童性虐待图像。
政治专家表示，爱泼斯坦受到竞选政客和选民的关注可能会减少，但这可能只是暂时的下降，而不是永久性的下降。
“确实感觉一切都着火了。我认为人们可以同时关心几件事，但直接影响他们生活的事情往往会被优先考虑，”担任“原则第一”代理主任的共和党策略师布列塔尼·马丁内斯说。 “当他们担心汽油价格、生活成本以及政府是否为他们工作时，爱泼斯坦可能会退出当前的对话。
“我不认为这些问题或对答案的需求已经消失；它们只是在争夺注意力。所以我希望在一段时间内听到更少的信息，而不是看到它完全消失。”
“特朗普每天都有一些事情，”布法罗大学政治学系临床副教授肖恩·多纳休说。
对于多纳休来说，时机也起着关键作用。美国国会一直在休会，众议院没有议员，因此没有对爱泼斯坦文件透明度法案拟议的新版本进行任何讨论。这项名为《爱泼斯坦档案透明度法案 II》的法案旨在解决倡导者所说的当前欧洲自由贸易联盟的缺陷，例如缺乏执行机制。
多纳休说：“感觉每当国会重新开会时，这可能会再次成为一个问题，特别是如果民主党正在考虑控制国会的一个或两个参众两院。”
如果民主党如民意调查所示赢得众议院，多纳休预计他们将迅速“让共和党人陷入与爱泼斯坦对峙的境地”。 “民主党人从第一天起就准备开始调查。”

A new kind of economic populism is surging in both parties this year as voters search for a political party that can solve growing concerns about financial stability.

Right-wing populism in the U.S. once meant being against the socially liberal elites on the East Coast and in California. On the left, populism used to mean being against billionaires and big corporations. But in this midterm election, those definitions are getting scrambled and a new kind of economic populism may be converging from the left and the right. NPR's senior national political correspondent Mara Liasson has this report.
MARA LIASSON, BYLINE: You'd be forgiven if you thought the following ads were run by Democrats.
FRENCH HILL: Keep Wall Street from buying up our neighborhoods.
MIKE ROGERS: The pharmaceutical companies are ripping American families off.
JOE MITCHELL: Because politicians shouldn't get rich while Iowa families struggle to afford groceries, housing and childcare.

LIASSON: They sound like they were written by Bernie Sanders' media consultant, but French Hill, Mike Rogers and Joe Mitchell are all Republicans. Historians of populism, like Georgetown professor Michael Kazin, say Americans are more open to economic populism when they're feeling squeezed or worse.
MICHAEL KAZIN: Economic populism emerges when ordinary people believe that they're getting screwed, betrayed by economic elites.

LIASSON: This year's populism is bipartisan. It's why you see Steve Bannon and Bernie Sanders appear back-to-back at the same anti-AI conference, and it's reflected in poll after poll. Democratic pollster Celinda Lake surveyed 500 working-class Americans without college degrees and with incomes under $150,000. The poll was commissioned by the Friedrich Ebert Foundation, which is affiliated with the German Social Democratic Party.

CELINDA LAKE: What really surprises us is the number of people - about 40% - who are cynical about the American dream don't think it's possible anymore and are sarcastic about it, that it's gone. It's a lie. It's a false promise.

LIASSON: A false promise that if you worked hard and got an education, you could do as well or better than your parents. What also surprised Lake was that big majorities, 70%, blame extreme wealth inequality for ending the American dream. And the same big majorities, 69%, say the government has an obligation to address it. NPR's swing voter focus groups found the same thing. All our voters backed Biden in 2020, and then they all voted for Trump in 2024. They agreed to be part of the focus group on the condition that they would be identified by first name only. So here's Jennifer (ph), Tony (ph) and Jeff (ph).

JENNIFER: It seems like the most wealth in this country is held by such a small percentage of people. And then we have people, you know, really struggling, and I think it's getting harder and harder to reach that American dream and get where you need to be.

TONY: I have nothing against billionaires or people who are making money. But I think that a lot of our problems, economic problems, are stemming from those who can't get enough who don't want to pay taxes.

JEFF: There's a handful of people, maybe 10 people, that hold 50% of the wealth in the country. And if you do have that much money, you should be taxed heavily, and that should trickle down to everyday citizens.

今年，随着选民寻找一个能够解决人们日益增长的金融稳定担忧的政党，一种新型经济民粹主义在两党中兴起。
美国的右翼民粹主义曾经意味着反对东海岸和加利福尼亚州的社会自由派精英。在左翼看来，民粹主义过去意味着反对亿万富翁和大公司。但在这次中期选举中，这些定义正在变得混乱，一种新的经济民粹主义可能正在从左翼和右翼汇聚。 NPR 的高级国家政治记者 Mara Liasson 有这份报道。
玛拉·利亚森连线：如果您认为以下广告是由民主党投放的，那也情有可原。
FRENCH HILL：阻止华尔街收购我们的社区。
迈克·罗杰斯：制药公司正在欺骗美国家庭。
乔·米切尔：因为政客们不应该在爱荷华州的家庭努力负担食品杂货、住房和儿童保育费用的时候变得富有。
利亚森：它们听起来像是伯尼·桑德斯的媒体顾问写的，但弗伦奇·希尔、迈克·罗杰斯和乔·米切尔都是共和党人。乔治城大学教授迈克尔·卡辛等民粹主义历史学家表示，当美国人感到受到挤压或更糟时，他们对经济民粹主义更加开放。
迈克尔·卡津：当普通人相信自己被经济精英欺骗、背叛时，经济民粹主义就会出现。
利亚森：今年的民粹主义是两党共同的。这就是为什么你会看到史蒂夫·班农和伯尼·桑德斯连续出现在同一个反人工智能会议上，这在一次又一次的民意调查中得到了反映。民主党民意调查专家塞琳达·莱克 (Celinda Lake) 对 500 名没有大学学位、收入低于 15 万美元的美国工人阶级进行了调查。这项民意调查是由隶属于德国社会民主党的弗里德里希·艾伯特基金会委托进行的。
塞琳达·莱克：真正令我们惊讶的是，有多少人（大约 40%）对美国梦持愤世嫉俗的态度，认为美国梦不再可能，并讽刺美国梦已经消失。这是一个谎言。这是一个虚假的承诺。

利亚森：这是一个错误的承诺，即如果你努力工作并接受教育，你就可以做得和你的父母一样好，甚至更好。同样令莱克惊讶的是，大多数人（70%）将美国梦的终结归咎于极端的财富不平等。同样的大多数人（69%）表示政府有义务解决这个问题。 NPR 的摇摆选民焦点小组也发现了同样的情况。我们所有的选民在 2020 年都支持了拜登，然后在 2024 年他们都投票给了特朗普。他们同意成为焦点小组的成员，条件是只透露名字。这里是 Jennifer（博士）、Tony（博士）和 Jeff（博士）。
詹妮弗：这个国家的大部分财富似乎都掌握在一小部分人手中。然后我们的人们，你知道，真的在挣扎，我认为实现美国梦和到达你需要去的地方变得越来越难。
托尼：我并不反对亿万富翁或赚钱的人。但我认为我们的很多问题，经济问题，都源于那些得不到足够的收入而不想纳税的人。
杰夫：少数人，也许 10 个人，掌握着这个国家 50% 的财富。如果你确实有那么多钱，你应该缴纳重税，这应该惠及普通公民。
